title: He viajado
goal: Talk about experiences and what you have or haven't done yet, with the present perfect.

lessons.title: I have spoken
lessons.notes:
The **present perfect** works much like English "I have done": **haber** + a **participle**.
**haber** (only used as a helper here):
**yo** he · **tú** has · **él / ella / usted** ha · **nosotros** hemos · **ellos / ustedes** han
The participle: **-ar -> -ado**, **-er / -ir -> -ido**: hablado, comido, vivido.
**He comido.** = I have eaten.
The participle never changes (no -a, no -s) after haber, and nothing goes between **he** and it: **no** and pronouns go in front: **No lo he visto.** = I haven't seen it.
**Spain vs Latin America:** in Spain, things done **today** go in the present perfect: **Hoy he trabajado mucho.** Most of Latin America uses the preterite there: **Hoy trabajé mucho.** Both are right; you'll be understood either way.

items.note: he, has, ha, hemos, han + participle.

sentences.es: He hablado con el médico esta semana.
sentences.en: I've spoken with the doctor this week.
accept_en: I have spoken to the doctor this week.
I spoke with the doctor this week.
I've talked to the doctor this week.

sentences.es: ¿Has comido? - Sí, he comido pollo.
sentences.en: Have you eaten? - Yes, I've had chicken.
accept_en: Have you eaten? - Yes, I've eaten chicken.
Did you eat? - Yes, I had chicken.

sentences.es: Carlos ha llegado hoy de Chile.
sentences.en: Carlos has arrived from Chile today.
accept_en: Carlos has arrived today from Chile.

sentences.es: Hemos vivido aquí diez años.
sentences.en: We've lived here for ten years.
accept_en: We have lived here for ten years.

sentences.es: Mis padres han trabajado mucho este año.
sentences.en: My parents have worked a lot this year.
accept_en: My parents worked a lot this year.

sentences.es: Esta semana he estado muy ocupado.
sentences.en: This week I've been very busy.
accept_en: I've been very busy this week.
I have been very busy this week.
This week I was very busy.

sentences.es: Hoy no he comido nada.
sentences.en: I haven't eaten anything today.

sentences.es: Ana ha estado enferma toda la semana.
sentences.en: Ana has been sick all week.
accept_en: Ana has been ill all week.

lessons.title: Irregular participles
lessons.notes:
A handful of common verbs have irregular participles. They're worth learning as words:
**hacer** -> **hecho** (done, made) · **ver** -> **visto** (seen) · **decir** -> **dicho** (said)
**escribir** -> **escrito** · **poner** -> **puesto** (put) · **volver** -> **vuelto** (come back)
**abrir** -> **abierto** (opened) · **romper** -> **roto** (broken) · **morir** -> **muerto** (died)
**¿Qué has hecho hoy?** = What have you done today?
Verbs ending in vowel + -er / -ir add an accent: **leído**, **oído**, **traído**.
You can also use a participle as an adjective, and then it agrees: **la ventana está abierta**, **los vasos están rotos**.

sentences.es: ¿Qué has hecho hoy?
sentences.en: What have you done today?

sentences.es: ¿Has visto mis gafas?
sentences.en: Have you seen my glasses?

sentences.es: Me ha dicho que no puede venir.
sentences.en: He's told me he can't come.
accept_en: She's told me she can't come.
He told me that he can't come.
She has told me that she can't come.

sentences.es: He escrito tres mensajes a Luis.
sentences.en: I've written three messages to Luis.
accept_en: I have written Luis three messages.
I wrote three messages to Luis.

sentences.es: ¿Dónde has puesto las llaves?
sentences.en: Where have you put the keys?
accept_en: Where did you put the keys?

sentences.es: Mi hermano ha vuelto de México.
sentences.en: My brother has come back from Mexico.
accept_en: My brother has returned from Mexico.
My brother came back from Mexico.

sentences.es: ¿Quién ha abierto la ventana?
sentences.en: Who has opened the window?

sentences.es: El niño ha roto un vaso.
sentences.en: The boy has broken a glass.
accept_en: The child has broken a glass.

sentences.es: He leído ese libro dos veces.
sentences.en: I've read that book twice.
accept_en: I have read that book twice.
I've read that book two times.

sentences.es: Rompí mis gafas ayer.
sentences.en: I broke my glasses yesterday.

lessons.title: Already, not yet
lessons.notes:
The present perfect goes with time words that reach up to **now**:
**ya** (already) · **todavía no** (not yet) · **todavía** (still) · **nunca** (never) · **alguna vez** (ever)
**¿Ya has comido?** = Have you eaten yet / already?
**Todavía no he terminado.** = I haven't finished yet.
In Latin America people often use the preterite with **ya**: **¿Ya comiste?** - it's just as correct.
**todavía** without **no** means "still": **Todavía vivo en el mismo barrio.**
**acabar de** + infinitive = to have just done: **Acabo de llegar.** = I've just arrived.

sentences.es: ¿Ya has comido? - Sí, ya he comido.
sentences.en: Have you eaten yet? - Yes, I've already eaten.
accept_en: Have you already eaten? - Yes, I've already eaten.
Did you eat yet? - Yes, I already ate.

sentences.es: Todavía no he terminado la tarea.
sentences.en: I haven't finished the homework yet.
accept_en: I still haven't finished my homework.
I haven't finished my homework yet.

sentences.es: ¿Ya contestaste el correo de Marta?
sentences.en: Have you answered Marta's email yet?
accept_en: Did you answer Marta's email yet?
Have you already replied to Marta's email?

sentences.es: Todavía vivo en el mismo barrio.
sentences.en: I still live in the same neighbourhood.
accept_en: I still live in the same neighborhood.
I still live in the same area.

sentences.es: Acabo de llegar a casa.
sentences.en: I've just got home.

sentences.es: El tren acaba de salir.
sentences.en: The train has just left.

sentences.es: ¿Todavía estás en la oficina?
sentences.en: Are you still at the office?
accept_en: Are you still in the office?

sentences.es: Mi hijo todavía no ha vuelto.
sentences.en: My son hasn't come back yet.
accept_en: My son still hasn't come back.

sentences.es: Ya he contestado todas las preguntas.
sentences.en: I've already answered all the questions.
accept_en: I have already answered all the questions.

lessons.title: Have you ever...?
lessons.notes:
Life experiences - things you have or haven't done at some point - use the present perfect everywhere:
**¿Alguna vez has estado en Chile?** = Have you ever been to Chile?
**Nunca he probado el mate.** = I've never tried mate.
**He estado en México dos veces.** = I've been to Mexico twice.
**ir** -> **ido**, **ser** -> **sido**: **He ido a Lima.** (I've been to Lima.)
In English "been to" is about places; in Spanish say **he estado en** or **he ido a**.
**muchas veces** = many times; **varias veces** = several times.

items.note: en el extranjero = abroad; also a foreigner.

sentences.es: ¿Alguna vez has estado en Chile?
sentences.en: Have you ever been to Chile?
accept_en: Have you ever been in Chile?

sentences.es: Nunca he probado la comida peruana.
sentences.en: I've never tried Peruvian food.
accept_en: I have never tried Peruvian food.

sentences.es: He ido a México muchas veces.
sentences.en: I've been to Mexico many times.
accept_en: I have been to Mexico many times.
I've gone to Mexico lots of times.

sentences.es: Ha sido un año muy difícil.
sentences.en: It's been a very hard year.
accept_en: It has been a very difficult year.
It's been a really difficult year.

sentences.es: Hemos subido esa montaña varias veces.
sentences.en: We've climbed that mountain several times.
accept_en: We have climbed that mountain several times.
We've been up that mountain several times.

sentences.es: ¿Has vivido alguna vez en el extranjero?
sentences.en: Have you ever lived abroad?

sentences.es: Nunca he visto la nieve.
sentences.en: I've never seen snow.

sentences.es: Mi abuela nunca ha subido a un avión.
sentences.en: My grandmother has never been on a plane.
accept_en: My grandma has never got on a plane.

sentences.es: ¿Cuántas veces has ido a la playa este año?
sentences.en: How many times have you been to the beach this year?
accept_en: How many times have you gone to the beach this year?
